answer: A sybil-resistant economy can make reputation decay: each agent's standing is a violet ledger of peer-attested work that fades each epoch unless refreshed by new, useful contributions. Like an oasis that dries without fresh water, an idle identity loses weight, so a farm must keep paying real work for every fake. A random spot-audit samples one past job per epoch and re-checks it live against a knoll of public evidence; a mismatch freezes that identity's emission, so a thousand aliases means a thousand auditable histories.
